summary: Prof.kaya@aegean.edu has one confirmed sign-in from Turkcell (TR) outside baseline via non-interactive mail-sync token (ExchangeSync/15), not the account holder (F2). The remaining sign-ins come from Portugal over university VPN vpn-edge-02 on device LT-3104 (F3). Rejected claims—impossible travel, password spray from shared egress IP, and KEV-listed VPNs—do not establish account abuse. The Risk Gate escalates because one access signal exists without a confirmed abuse chain, per evidence policy.

risk.rationale: All verified signals for prof.kaya@aegean.edu have innocent, context-consistent explanations. The single confirmed out-of-baseline Turkcell (TR) event (F2, T1078.004, conf 0.75) is a non-interactive ExchangeSync/15 mail-sync token, not an interactive logon by the account holder; Turkcell is a Turkish carrier and Aegean University is in Turkey, so this is consistent with a mobile device on the home network rather than an intruder. The frequent Portugal sign-ins (F3, lik 0.5) traverse the university VPN vpn-edge-02 from known device LT-3104, not an unknown actor. The alleged impossible travel is rejected because the TR event is non-interactive and the PT logins are VPN-mediated. The alleged password spray from 193.140.10.21 is background noise on a shared egress IP (201 distinct accounts completed MFA from it in 30 days; 60 failures across 54 accounts is not coordinated). KEV concerns are neutralized: vpn-edge-02 firmware 22.7R2.8 already contains the cited fixes, and vpn-edge-01 never authenticated this account. No confirmed account-takeover chain, no data-quality conflicts, and no unresolved exposure. Suspicious signals are explained away -> benign.
